claims.content: The EW-capable C2 JU determines which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG, either manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
The C2 JU transmits lines of bearing (LOBs), fixes, or areas of probability (AOPs) via the J3.7 EW Product Information message on the Surveillance Network PG.
The C2 JU may amplify LOBs, fixes, and AOPs by the J6.0 Amplification message on the Surveillance Network PG.
The C2 JU reports EW association using the J7.7 message.
The C2 JU may use the J7.2 message to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.
When the C2 JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

A1. At step 0, the determination of which EW detections are eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG may be performed manually or through automatic association with predetermined reporting criteria.
A2. At step 1, if data are available, additional continuation words may be added to the minimum required word sequences to amplify EW reports.

A3. At step 1, when SIM = 1 and the applicable ENV, ID, GEO, and SP flag combination matches a defined inhibition condition, the EW Product is inhibited from transmission (e.g., SIM=1, ENV=0, ID=0, GEO=0, SP=0 inhibits any EW Product with Simulation status).

A4. At step 1, if an AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, assign a new TN not one of the TNs assigned to the fixes and use the new TN for all subsequent updates; if a fix is changed to an AOP, use the TN of the previously reported fix for the new AOP.

A5. At step 1, a JU with R^2 shall initiate an emergency or force tell alert on EW Product information by setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in the J3.7 message, and all receiving JUs shall accept the alert in their databases.

A6. At step 1, the JU with R^2 shall terminate an emergency or force tell alert by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert and setting the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in subsequent J3.7 messages to 0; all receiving JUs shall terminate the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message; optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with the EMG and/or FT IND set to value 0.
A7. At step 4, the J7.2 message may be used to correlate EW AOPs with surveillance tracks, but the J7.2 message shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.

A8. At step 5, the transmission of EW product information shall be terminated when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met; the information may be purged in accordance with system design.

A9. At step 5, when a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message; the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted on remote reports, and remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.

E1. If SIM = 1 and the applicable ENV, ID, GEO, and SP flag combination matches a defined EW Product inhibition condition, inhibit transmission of that EW Product and exit this use case for that EW Product.

E2. If the EW product information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met, terminate transmission of that EW product information; the information may be purged in accordance with system design; exit this use case for that EW product information.
E3. If the C2 JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and exit this use case for that EW information.

E4. If the EW information being dropped or ceased is a remote report, do not transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on remote reports; remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria; exit this exception without transmitting J7.0 (ACT = 0).

E5. If correlation of EW LOBs or fixes with surveillance tracks is attempted via the J7.2 message, do not use J7.2 for that correlation because J7.2 shall not be used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks; report EW association using the J7.7 message and exit this exception.
EW detections eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG have resulted in the transmission of LOBs, AOPs, or fixes.
The unit originating the J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report retains reporting responsibility.
EW association is reported using the J7.7 message.
If the J7.2 message is used, it correlates EW AOPs with surveillance tracks and is not used to correlate EW LOBs and fixes with surveillance tracks.

If an AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, the AOP is assigned a new TN not one of the TNs assigned to the fixes, and the new TN is used for all subsequent updates of the AOP; if a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix is used for the new AOP.

If a JU with R^2 initiated an emergency or force tell alert on EW Product information, the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND is set in the J3.7 message, and all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases.

If a JU with R^2 terminated an emergency or force tell alert, a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert has been transmitted, the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in subsequent J3.7 messages is set to 0, and all receiving JUs have terminated the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message; optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.7 message with the EMG and/or FT IND set to value 0.
Transmission of EW product information that is no longer valid or does not meet time-related update requirements has been terminated; the information may be purged in accordance with system design.

When a JU drops or ceases reporting EW information that it has been reporting on the interface, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been transmitted, except the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted on remote reports and remote reports may be automatically purged based on system criteria.
